plain_description.what: Estimating each model's accuracy from only 100 sampled questions. Sampling is spread evenly across the tree's cells, then compared with plain random sampling, sampling by benchmark source, and sampling by per-source k-means groups. Done on 5,907 held-out questions with 18 models, each model left out in turn.
plain_description.why: If the tree's cells capture what makes questions differ, sampling by cell should give accurate scores from fewer questions, which would make evaluation cheaper.
plain_description.information: A clear win over source sampling would support 'the tree cuts evaluation cost'. Result (no new calls): sampling by tree cell beats plain random sampling (about 5% lower error). It is not better than per-source k-means groups, and it cannot be told apart from sampling by source (undetermined, below what the test could detect), for the tree as built. So no 'the tree makes evaluation cheaper' claim is made.
